newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ITC posts record six-month net profit.
newsitem.headline: India's ITC posts record six-month net profit.

text.p: Indian tobacco and hotel group ITC Ltd reported on Monday a record first-half net profit which it said was driven by solid growth in its core tobacco and hotel businesses.

Net profit jumped 28 percent to 1.81 billion rupees ($50.7 million) in the first six months of the 1996/97 financial year which began on April 1, up from 1.41 billion rupees in the same period last year, the company said in a statement.
ITC said the first-half net profit was a record. It did not say what the previous record was and company officials could not be reached for comment.

The Calcutta-based company released the results against the backdrop of a widening government probe into alleged foreign exchange violations. Twelve current and former ITC employees have been detained in the case.
Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc is the biggest single shareholder in ITC with a 31.7 percent stake.
The results were officially announced after the Bombay Stock Exchange closed.

But speculation that ITC was likely to report stronger-than-expected net profit of about 1.8 billion rupees helped the overall share market recover from a near-four percent plunge in early trading, analysts said.
ITC shares slid to a low of 264 on the Bombay bourse on Monday before a late recovery drove them to 275.75 at the close, down 2.00 rupees on last Friday's finish.
ITC said in a statement released in New Delhi that the strong performance of its core businesses and growth potential augured well for years to come.
"With its investment and business strategies well in place, ITC looks ahead to a bright future," the statement said.
Net income rose 19 percent to 14.19 billion rupees in the first half while trading margins rose to 31 percent from 26 percent, it said.
ITC said that by the end of September, it had paid 3.2 billion rupees in owed excise duty out of 3.5 billion which must be paid to the government by next year.

The Central Excise Gold and Appellate Tribunal (CEGAT) in March ordered ITC to pay 3.5 billion rupees in excise duty for the period between March 1983 and February 1987. The payment is due by January 1, 1997.
"The referred CEGAT order will be fully complied with by the due date," ITC said. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
